reasons.plausibility: Partially replacing a high-electronegativity element (Mo) with a lower-electronegativity element (Nb) to reduce lattice distortion and improve ductility without drastically compromising strength is scientifically plausible and aligns with known principles of solid solution design, although the exact effect depends on phase stability and solid-solution strengthening behavior.
reasons.testability: The hypothesis outlines a clear experimental matrix (varying Mo replacement levels) and standard mechanical and structural characterization methods that would definitively validate or refute the predicted improvements in ductility and retention of strength.
reasons.usefulness: Addressing the trade-off between strength and ductility in this alloy system is highly relevant, and the proposed substitution strategy is directly actionable and could provide valuable guidance for optimizing high-entropy alloys.
